description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of three quality scoring methods—IFD, TagNum, and DEITA—on two distinct metrics: Avg_obj (represented by light blue bars) and Avg_sub (represented by light orange bars), as evaluated in the context of the paper “MIG Automatic Data Selection for Instruction Tuning by Maximizing Information Gain in Semantic Space.” The vertical axis, labeled “Scores,” ranges from 30 to 70 in increments of 5, while the horizontal axis, labeled “Quality Scores,” categorizes the three methods. For IFD, Avg_obj achieves a score of 63.98 and Avg_sub scores 41.90; for TagNum, Avg_obj is 66.06 and Avg_sub is 39.13; for DEITA, Avg_obj reaches 67.64 and Avg_sub is 42.99. A dashed blue horizontal line at approximately 64.71 represents the “Base Avg_obj” baseline, while a dashed orange line near 37.91 indicates the “Base Avg_sub” baseline. The chart visually emphasizes that DEITA yields the highest Avg_obj score among the three methods, while IFD and DEITA outperform TagNum on Avg_sub, with DEITA achieving the highest Avg_sub score overall. The legend in the upper right corner clarifies the color coding and baseline references, and all bars are labeled with their exact numerical values for precision.
